paper.title_en: A cross-domain empirical benchmark of quantum-inspired and classical optimization algorithms for machine learning
paper.abstract_en: Quantum-inspired (QI) optimizers are increasingly proposed as alternatives to classical gradient-based training, yet are frequently benchmarked through classical stand-ins rather than themselves. Across tabular, vision, and language tasks we evaluate three classes: direct implementations of published update rules (Spall's SPSA; quantum-behaved particle swarm optimization, QPSO, adapted to stochastic minibatches), a documented classical analog of quantum natural gradient (an NGD-style diagonal second-moment preconditioner), and the hyperparameter-control configurations under which such methods are often reported. The gap between these classes is our central result: on the tabular benchmark the hyperparameter control trains with the classical baselines while the direct algorithms fall $\approx $10-24 points below it, and on CIFAR-10/ResNet18, where v1's "SPSA" arm was a learning-rate-scaled Adam, Adam itself stands $\approx $59 points above genuine SPSA. The QPSO adaptation stays at chance on LSTM tasks a legacy "QPSO" proxy solves at 79-81%, at 18-38$\times $ Adam's cost there and up to 74$\times $ on the small CV model. A seed-paired $2\times 2$ factorial on RoBERTa identifies the smaller learning rate as the dominant observed component of the earlier "QNG advantage" ($+0.50$ points at the dataset level); with only three datasets, modified Hartung-Knapp uncertainty spans zero. The configured NGD arm shows no detectable advantage over a learning-rate-matched AdamW (descriptive pooled $p{=}0.23$) at 6-$7\%$ extra cost, and on ResNet18 its trained endpoints have larger dominant-curvature estimates than the Adam family's. Headline comparisons use five seeds, paired tests, Holm correction, and stated detection limits. We conclude with an auditing taxonomy (direct algorithm / analog / hyperparameter control): within the arms, protocols, and scales evaluated, no advantage attributable to a QI mechanism is detected after these controls.
